question: What will be the ending value of the ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread for these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Last print 2.70 on 2026-09-17; the series has held a 2.60-2.87 band for four months and 2.65-2.76 all of September. Status quo for an 11-business-day horizon in a daily credit-spread series is a near-random-walk, so the prior median is the last value; I shade to 2.71 for the mid-September firming (2.76 on the 15th) and a mild upward tilt from starting in the richest decile of the series' history, where mean reversion is one-directional. Known in-window catalysts are thin: the Sep 16 FOMC hike to 3.75-4.00% is already absorbed and no meeting falls in the window, and the Oct 1 shutdown risk was removed by the Sep 2 CR funding through Dec 11. The right tail is the asymmetry that matters - Fitch's record 6.3% private-credit default rate, and the Oct 2025 precedent where this same calendar window took the OAS from 2.76 to 3.18 - while the left is floored by the 2.41 all-time low 30bp away. No human prediction market prices this contract (checked Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi; Polymarket's bond board is yield-level contracts only), so there is no crowd anchor. I kept the 10-90 width at the reference-class figure rather than clipping it to the calmer realized band of the last four months.

calls.reconciliation: The three runs agreed on the resolution instrument (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, not an ETF price, not Bloomberg HY 2% Issuer Capped), on the anchor (2.70 on 2026-09-17), on the resolving observation (Oct 1, given FRED's one-business-day lag), on the absence of an Oct 1 shutdown (CR signed 2026-09-02 funds through Dec 11), on the absence of an in-window FOMC, and on the absence of any human market. Four disputes remained. (1) Horizon: 11 vs 9-10 business days - settled by counting Sep 18 through Oct 1 inclusive = 10; immaterial to dispersion. (2) Mid-September rates/equity tape: Run 1 (10y 4.78%, equity levels from a podcast recap) vs Run 3 (10y near 5%, risk-off) vs Run 2 (S&P -0.1%, Dow -1.7%, Nasdaq +0.7% from a dated wrap). No web access this run, so this could not be settled; it is also close to moot, because OAS is a spread over Treasuries and the series itself went 2.76 -> 2.70 -> 2.70 straight through the hike with CCCs outperforming BBs, which is a rates move rather than a credit-quality move. I note that Run 2 independently flagged Run 1's equity source as an unrelated options podcast whose index levels conflict with a dated wrap, and I have given that source no weight. (3) Series all-time low, 2.33 vs 2.41 - unsettleable here and irrelevant, since both sit far below the 1.745 bound and neither creates a low-side mechanism. (4) Judgment dispute on dispersion basis: calm-last-two-months SD ~0.08 (width ~0.20) vs trailing-12m SD ~0.12 (width ~0.30). I carry the trailing-12m basis forward, agreeing with all three runs, because the window covers quarter-end and the October turn and because Feb-Mar 2026 demonstrates how quickly this regime breaks; clipping to the calm band is the known under-dispersion failure. On the median, no evidence breaks the 2.70-vs-2.71 tie: Run 2's own class implies a median change of -0.03, which points down, but that reflects two years of net compression that cannot extrapolate from the richest decile of the series' history. I take flat-plus-a-hair, 2.71, as the reading I would bet on. This is not an average of the runs - it is the status-quo number their shared evidence supports, with the right skew coming from a compressed left tail (2.60 three weeks ago, modern floor ~30bp under it) rather than from splitting differences.

disagreements.claim: Probability of clearing the 3.505 upper bound
disagreements.verdict: All three independently priced 1% and the base rate supports it: zero of ~49 same-length windows in two years produced the required +80bp, and the sole episode capable of it (April 2025) began from an exogenous shock with no analogue on the in-window calendar. Held at 0.01.

disagreements.claim: Whether any human market anchors this question
disagreements.verdict: Settled and unanimous: three independent checks of Polymarket, Manifold and Kalshi found only yield-level and macro-event contracts, never a credit-spread level. No crowd blend applied.
